editorial:
Here is a strange and bold film from director Yorgos Lanthimos. It tells three separate stories, all starring the same actors in different roles. In the first, a man fights to take control of his life from a boss who runs everything. In the second, a cop doubts his wife after she returns from being lost at sea. In the third, a cult member searches for someone who can bring people back to life. The vibe is dark, funny, and deeply weird, with a dry sense of humor that keeps you guessing.

The acting is the real highlight. Emma Stone, Jesse Plemons, and Willem Dafoe are fantastic, shifting between roles with ease. The pacing is slow and deliberate, which some viewers will love and others will find tiring. Pros: great performances, unique stories, and a bold style. Cons: it is long, odd, and not for everyone. If you enjoy strange, thought-provoking films, this is for you.
endingExplained: In the final story, Emily is kicked out of the cult after failing to resurrect Ruth, who died in a car crash. She drives off alone, still searching for someone with the special power. The movie ends on a dark, open note, suggesting the cycle of control and obsession will continue. Across all three tales, the characters never truly break free, and the mysterious R.M.F. keeps appearing, tying the fables together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves strange, thought-provoking films with great acting.
